hints: The final sequence must be nondecreasing, but values can move in both directions.
When a smaller value appears, earlier choices that are too large may need to decrease.
A max-heap tracks the largest adjustable values.
analogy: Think of a descending bump being flattened by lowering an earlier height and raising the current one toward the same level.
algorithm: Scan the array with a max-heap and a 64-bit answer. Insert the current value x. If the heap maximum is greater than x, remove that maximum y, add y-x to the answer, and insert x again. After the scan, print the answer.
correctness: This is the slope-trick form of L1 isotonic regression. After each prefix, the heap stores breakpoints of the minimum cost as a function of its allowed final value. Inserting x adds the absolute-deviation cost; replacing a maximum y>x with x enforces the nondecreasing constraint and adds the unavoidable gap y-x. Induction over prefixes gives the minimum total adjustment cost.
complexity: For n values, each heap operation takes O(log n), so time is O(n log n) and space O(n).
